final_recommendation: The room failed to converge on a negotiated settlement. Despite FINMA offering a Wednesday subordination statement and 45-day discovery closure, bondholder counsel issued a multi-jurisdiction filing ultimatum when the methodology annex deadline passed unmet, reverting to litigation as the dominant path.
minority_objections: Credit market analyst repeatedly warned that litigation velocity (5-year appeals tail) would outlast market patience, arguing spreads would relock regardless of legal wins
Institutional investor threatened exit by Friday if settlement framework didn't close by mid-May, viewing litigation as destroying residual AT1 market confidence
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel demanded full board-and-adviser E&O release framework as non-negotiable; FINMA refused to release its own staff from discovery, creating irreconcilable positions on claims tail scope
Settlement velocity vs. market confidence: counsel needed 90-day window to validate proportionality numbers; investors needed signed term sheet by mid-May to prevent portfolio liquidation
Methodology annex timing: counsel made May 15 settlement close contingent on 4pm annex delivery; FINMA could not meet deadline, triggering litigation reversion
key_concessions: FINMA agreed to publish subordination doctrine statement by Wednesday affirming AT1 rank below equity and requiring independent viability verification before write-down
FINMA offered sealed confidentiality protocol for depositions and 45-day discovery closure timeline
Bondholder counsel initially agreed to table Monday filing for 90-day settlement window contingent on release framework delivery
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: full board-and-adviser E&O release framework or no settlement; 70% recovery floor non-negotiable
FINMA: cannot release own staff from pre-write-down discovery without undermining legal basis of emergency authority
Institutional investor: must see signed settlement term sheet by mid-May or exits AT1 class entirely
Bondholder counsel: methodology annex must lock by 4pm same day as statement or multi-jurisdiction filing proceeds
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Reputational damage to Swiss financial center from protracted multi-year litigation across three jurisdictions
Contagion to other European AT1 markets beyond Credit Suisse if hierarchy inversion precedent remains unresolved
Political/regulatory pressure on FINMA from SNB and Federal Department of Finance if litigation exposes internal proportionality decision-making
Operational risk that 45-day discovery closure timeline was unrealistic given multi-party coordination requirements
downstream_risk_variables: AT1 spread trajectory through Q2-Q3 2023 if litigation proceeds without settlement framework
New issuance volumes for European banks' AT1 capital raises in H2 2023
E&O and D&O claims frequency and severity against Credit Suisse board and external advisers through 2024-2025
Reinsurance accumulation exposure if multiple European banks face parallel AT1 creditor challenges
FINMA's ability to invoke emergency authority in future bank resolutions without triggering immediate legal challenge
uncertainty_notes: The room terminated without resolving whether FINMA's Wednesday statement would actually stabilize AT1 spreads absent a signed settlement, whether the 45-day discovery timeline was operationally feasible, and whether the methodology annex was truly a hard blocker or negotiating leverage. The litigation filing ultimatum left open whether counsel would actually proceed Monday or use the threat for final concessions.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Multi-jurisdiction filing ultimatum issued in R8 after annex deadline passed; 48-hour notice of intent and 60-day proportionality timer dominated R1-R4; litigation reversion was the terminal outcome
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: FINMA's Article 36 emergency authority and 19 March ordinance challenged as retroactive rewrite (R1-R2), but room focused more on procedural proportionality breach than fundamental legitimacy of viability-event basis
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Equity-preserved-while-AT1-wiped inversion was the foundational grievance driving 70% recovery demand and subordination statement requirement; hierarchy restoration was counsel's stated non-negotiable (R1, R3, R4)
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 spread widening (50bps/week, 300+ locked), new issuance freeze, and capital market contagion were central threads in every round; institutional investor's exit threat and analyst's warnings drove settlement urgency
marker_evidence.claims_tail: E&O/D&O discovery tail (board, advisers, FINMA staff depositions) was developed across R3-R8 as multi-year, multi-party risk; release framework negotiations and 45-day closure timeline were core to settlement structure
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: Insurance observer raised D&O/E&O exposure and defense cost duration (18-month tail, Q4 2023 extension) in R3, R6-R8, but it remained a supporting concern rather than driving the room's direction

node: Node 2 - AT1 Creditor Reaction Room (late March 2023, AFTER the UBS rescue and the FINMA-ordered full write-down of Credit Suisse AT1 to zero were announced)
